text:
incident-bot: PAGING — streaming_tail_p99_ms for tenant citylane-prod in us-west-2 = 2400ms (SLO 1000ms). Sustained >3m. Triggered: streaming_stall_detector v2. Page: @oncall-jen @sre-ashley :rotating_light:

oncall-jen: Ack, on it. Creating thread for triage. I'll own mitigation until handoff.

ryan: Observed a big concurrency burst from a single API key tied to citylane-prod — concurrent streams ~420, request queue depth spiked to ~12k on vpool-usw2-gpu-3. A bunch of requests have very long prefixes (>5k tokens).

maria: Confirmed client reports: streaming starts (first chunk) then stalls for 5-12s before next chunk. p95 now ~650ms, p99 ~2400ms. Error rate up slightly (0.4% 5xx for that tenant).

eng-runtime: Attaching recent runtime logs from the impacted worker set (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] tenant=citylane-prod req_id=abc123 stage=enqueue queue_depth=11832
[2026-03-15T09:11:03Z] model=mistral-large shard=gpua-7 kvcache_hit=false latency_ms=1250 stream_chunks=1
[2026-03-15T09:11:05Z] warning: kvcache-pop thrash detected for prefix hash=0x9f2a client=citylane-prod
[2026-03-15T09:11:06Z] backpressure: inflight=420 max_inflight=2000
[2026-03-15T09:11:07Z] stall_detected req_id=abc123 stall_ms=5200
```

eng-runtime: Also seeing repeated long-token generation paths triggering attention kernel fallback which increases latency.

oncall-jen: Quick mitigation plan (ordered):
1) Route citylane-prod to fallback model variant (mistral-medium) for any streaming requests to reduce per-token latency.
2) Apply per-tenant concurrency cap at the routing layer (start with max_concurrency=25).
3) Increase KV cache TTL for the tenant's hot prefixes to reduce kvcache misses.
4) Temporarily disable streaming incremental chunking for this tenant (deliver full response once ready) to avoid frequent small wakes.
5) Notify Customer Success and the customer.

ryan: I'll prepare the routing patch and a k/v config update.

oncall-jen: Executing routing override now — patching control plane.

```
# apply tenant routing override
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routing/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant":"citylane-prod","overrides":{"streaming_fallback_model":"mistral-medium-v1","max_concurrency":25}}'

# quick k8s configmap edit (internal cluster)
kubectl -n redwood-routing patch configmap tenant-overrides --type merge -p '{"data":{"citylane-prod.max_concurrency":"25","citylane-prod.kvcache_ttl":"180s"}}'
```

incident-bot: routing override accepted, job_id=rte-7781, started rollout to us-west-2 pools.

sre-ashley: Picking this up — applying k/v cache TTL and disabling incremental streaming for tenant now.

eng-runtime: Observing immediate improvement after partial rollout: p99 trending down from 2400ms -> 980ms within 90s, p95 -> ~300ms. Some clients see 429s due to new concurrency cap (expected).

customer-success-alex: I'll send a short mitigation note to CityLane: "We've applied routing limits and a smaller model fallback to reduce latency. You may see rate limiting for heavy bursts. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a root-cause and timeline."

maria: Please capture sample prompts that triggered long prefixes for postmortem. Recommend saving top 50 hashed prefixes and the API key usage timeline.

eng-runtime: Sample prompt hashes (anonymized):
```
- phash:0x9f2a count:412 avg_len:5320
- phash:0x7c1b count:298 avg_len:4820
- phash:0xd4e1 count:87 avg_len:12000
```

oncall-jen: Impact summary for incident channel: CityLane production-only; duration from first alert to mitigation ~12m; partial mitigation effective ~3m after change; ~10% of CityLane streaming requests breached SLO during spike window. No cross-tenant spillover detected.

sre-ashley: Logged temporary changes in infra-ops runbook (will create PR to keep overrides tracked). Also enabled extra tracing on the routed workers: trace_level=debug for tenant=citylane-prod.

oncall-jen: Handoff: I'm off-shift in 28m. Passing to @sre-ashley. Notes for next on-call: watch for recurring long-prefix bursts from same API key, consider a throttle-by-prefix feature, follow up with CityLane to ask about client-side batching.

sre-ashley: ACK taking over. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/tenant-citylane-prod (keep this private). Will keep channel updated every 15m for next hour.

customer-success-alex: CityLane acknowledged, they're restricting a noisy integration on their side and will share client logs in 30m.

oncall-jen: Adding action items:
- [ ] eng-runtime: investigate kernel fallback path and optimize attention kernel selection for long prefixes (owner: ryan)
- [ ] platform: add per-tenant throttling policy to routing config UI + audit trail (owner: ashley)
- [ ] cs: collect customer logs and share safe sample prompts (owner: alex)
- [ ] sre: create incident doc + postmortem (owner: jen)

incident-bot: Status update -> mitigated; monitoring. If metrics regress above thresholds for another 10m, will escalate to Sev-1.

oncall-jen: Closing this paging thread, leaving monitoring to @sre-ashley. Please ping if anything changes. :thumbsup:

sre-ashley: Closing notes: mitigation stable at last check. Will open a follow-up for postmortem and remediation plan.
